tasks.title: Silence detection + cancel/re-issue core with shared once-only allowance (D56.1, D56.2-guard)
tasks.description: Add per-reqId last-activity stamps (monotonic clock, stamped at registration/issue, re-stamped on each accepted on_historical_bar), one session silence sweeper (1 s QTimer tick, armed only while history reqIds are in flight), and _retry_silent_chunk: plan lookup, cancel via the existing cancel path with superseded tagging and post-issue slot kept, drop of the old reqId, paced re-issue of the identical plan at the same plan position under the current generation with a new reqId, and recording in the shared _retried_plans allowance. Guard: plans already in _retried_plans are never silence-retried, and a re-issue's own silence never re-issues (no third issue). Zero-bar rule is primary; trailing-silence rule covers partial-then-stalled chunks (Q91).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given any issued history chunk reqId with zero bars received, no END, and no error for a continuous 30 s since issue, when the silence sweeper evaluates it, then that reqId is cancelled via the existing cancel path and the identical plan is re-issued exactly once at the same plan position under the current generation with a new reqId, and the re-issue's own 30 s window plus finalize margin conclude inside the 120 s watchdog bound.

AC2: Given any issued chunk that received at least one bar but then no further bar, END, or error for a trailing 30 s after the last accepted bar, when the bound is reached, then the same cancel plus exactly-once identical re-issue occurs; every accepted on_historical_bar re-stamps that reqId's last-activity clock, so a bar arriving at 30 s minus epsilon restarts the window and fires no retry.

AC3: Given any plan already present in the shared retry allowance (silence-retried or error-162-retried), when further 30 s silence elapses on its re-issue, then no further retry is issued for that plan — every chunk is issued at most twice per wave.

tests.description: Offscreen clock-controlled wave with one zero-bar-silent chunk: advance the clock past 30 s of silence with no END/error and assert cancelHistoricalData was called with the old reqId and exactly one identical re-issue exists (same symbol/timeframe/mode/span/plan position, new reqId, current generation); assert the in-flight set drops the old reqId and tracks the new one.
tests.expected_result: Exactly one cancel of the silent reqId plus one identical re-issue; no third issue; wave state consistent (old reqId untracked, new reqId in flight).

tests.description: Offscreen clock-controlled partial chunk (deliver 2 bars, then stall with no END/error): advance the clock 30 s past the last bar and assert the cancel plus exactly-once identical re-issue fires; in a second run deliver a bar at 29.9 s after the previous bar and assert no retry fires at 30 s from issue (trailing window restarted).
tests.expected_result: Stalled partial chunk retried exactly once; a bar at 30 s minus epsilon restarts the trailing window and fires no retry.

tests.description: Offscreen clock-controlled wave where the re-issued chunk is itself silent past 30 s under the same trigger rules: advance the clock through both windows and assert total issues per chunk equal exactly two and the sweeper skips plans already in _retried_plans.
tests.expected_result: No third issue for any chunk; _retried_plans contains the retried plan and the sweeper never re-selects it.

tests.description: Offscreen clock-controlled zero-bar chunk silent at 30 s minus epsilon then delivering a bar before the bound: assert no retry fires (single-sided bound) and the delivered bar is processed normally.
tests.expected_result: No cancel and no re-issue; the chunk proceeds on its first issue.

tasks.title: Generation fencing + identity-removal exactly-once counting (D56.4, D56.7-mechanism)
tasks.description: Make the supersede path fence late arrivals and count exactly once: when _retry_silent_chunk supersedes an old reqId, pop _req_bars[old] and remove exactly those Bar objects from _pending_bars by identity; late bars or ENDs arriving on the superseded reqId die at the unchanged _history_event_accepted fence with no count, persist, render, or wave-state change. Bars already persisted per-chunk stay in the cache (INSERT OR REPLACE PK-idempotent) and are re-read, never duplicated in memory.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given any bar or END arriving on a superseded (cancel-tagged, dropped from the in-flight set) reqId after the re-issue, then it is fenced: no bar is appended, persisted, or counted, and wave membership, counts, cache contents, and completion state are identical to the no-late-arrival case.

AC2: Given a silence retry superseding a partial chunk, then exactly the old reqId's Bar objects are removed from the in-memory wave totals by identity; bars already persisted per-chunk remain in the cache unchanged under the mode-aware PK and are re-read rather than duplicated in memory, so every chunk's bars count exactly once across both issues.

tests.description: Offscreen wave: retry a silent chunk, then deliver late bars plus a late END on the superseded reqId; assert bar counts, cache contents, and wave/completion state equal a control run with no late arrivals (fenced, no resurrection, no double-count).
tests.expected_result: Late arrivals on the superseded reqId change nothing: counts, cache rows, and wave state match the fenced expectation.

tests.description: Offscreen wave: partial chunk (N bars, one per-chunk persist) retried, re-issue yields the same N bars; assert the in-memory wave total credits each bar exactly once and the cache holds one row per (symbol, timeframe, ts) with a clean re-read.
tests.expected_result: In-memory totals count each bar once across both issues; cache rows are PK-unique and unchanged by the identical re-fetch.

tasks.title: Error taxonomy + pacing gate for the retry (D56.3, D56.5)
tasks.description: Generalise the cancel-ack rule in MainWindow._on_error so an error of any inventoried historical-request code (162, 321, 200, 399, 504) arriving on a cancel-tagged superseded reqId is debug-only with no status-bar message, no shortfall entry, and no pacing event; errors on the fresh re-issued reqId keep existing semantics with the shared _retried_plans allowance checked first (a 162 on a silence-retried chunk finalizes short, never a third issue). Route the re-issue through paced req_historical_data; on PacingExceeded wait via the existing continuation path bounded by the unchanged watchdog (watchdog-first yields counted stranded fall-through, fail-open). Both reqIds consume pacing slots (post-issue cancels keep their slots; no refund).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given an error of any inventoried historical-request code arriving on a cancel-tagged superseded reqId, then it is classified as a cancel acknowledgement (debug-level only: no status-bar message, no shortfall entry, no pacing event); given an error on the fresh re-issued reqId, then existing error semantics apply with the shared allowance checked first, so a 162 on an already-silence-retried plan finalizes short with no third issue.

AC2: Given a silence retry, then both the cancelled and the re-issued reqIds consume pacing slots (a post-issue cancel keeps its slot — no refund); given no pacing slot frees before the watchdog horizon, then the wave falls through to the unchanged watchdog strand-finalization (fail-open and counted) and no historical request is ever issued outside the pacing budget.

tests.description: Offscreen error injection parametrized over every inventoried code (162, 321, 200, 399, 504) on a cancel-tagged superseded reqId: assert debug-only handling with no status-bar message, no shortfall entry, and no pacing event for every code.
tests.expected_result: Every inventoried code on a superseded reqId classifies as cancel-ack with zero user-facing or budget effect.

tests.description: Offscreen: inject a 162 on the re-issued (silence-retried) reqId and assert the chunk finalizes short under existing error semantics with total issues per chunk staying at exactly two.
tests.expected_result: Fresh-reqId 162 on an already-retried plan finalizes short; no third issue.

tests.description: Offscreen pacing-spy wave with one silent chunk: assert both the cancelled and the re-issued reqIds consumed pacing slots and the post-issue cancel refunded nothing.
tests.expected_result: Two slots consumed for the retried chunk; no refund on the post-issue cancel.

tests.description: Offscreen: force PacingExceeded at re-issue time with no slot freeing before the watchdog horizon; assert the wave falls through to the unchanged watchdog strand-finalization (counted) and no unpaced request is issued.
tests.expected_result: Pacing exhaustion yields counted watchdog fall-through; the rolling budget is never violated.

tasks.title: Prime-retry wall-clock flake hardening, test-only (ESC-100)
tasks.description: Harden test_p7_t07_t13_prime_retry_defers_then_issues against the ~1.7% wall-clock boundary flake: _on_prime_retry re-enters prime_aggregator with int(time.time()), so a run landing in the first 5 s of a 300 s period takes the span_s<5 fail-open path and _prime_req_id stays None. Freeze the retry clock in-test and add a deterministic period-boundary case pinning the fail-open path. Test-only: no production file is modified, no assertion is weakened, P17 never touches the prime path.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given the prime retry deferred with pacing closed, then when _on_prime_retry runs with the clock frozen at a mid-period instant (span_s>=5 deterministically regardless of wall-clock phase) the retry issues exactly once (_prime_req_id set, pending cleared) on every run with zero wall-clock dependence; Given the clock frozen at a period-boundary instant (span_s<5), then the retry deterministically takes the existing fail-open path (no issue, skip counted, live feed attached) with no production-code change and no weakened assertion.

tests.description: Revise test_p7_t07_t13_prime_retry_defers_then_issues to freeze the clock (monkeypatch time.time as seen by ui.ticker_session to the existing mid_period_ts() instant) across the _on_prime_retry() call and assert issue-once with _prime_req_id set and pending cleared; add test_p7_t07_t13_prime_retry_boundary_fail_open_deterministic freezing the clock at period_start+1 s (span_s<5) asserting no issue (_prime_req_id None), skip counted, fail-open completion. Run the full tests/test_p7_w4_streaming.py module green plus a 20x loop of the revised defers-then-issues test to prove determinism.
tests.expected_result: Revised test passes on every run regardless of wall-clock phase; boundary case deterministically pins fail-open; no other test in the module regresses.
